item.title: ✈️ #Announcement The highly anticipated Africa Aerospace and Defence ( #AAD ) Expo 2026
item.description: #Announcement ✈️ ✨ The highly anticipated Africa Aerospace and Defence ( #AAD ) Expo 2026 has officially kicked off its massive five-day run today at Air Force Base Waterkloof today. 🇿🇦 Celebrating a milestone 25th anniversary , this premier global exhibition is transforming the City of Tshwane, Pretoria, into the epicenter of aviation and defense industry from September 16 to 20 . Over 30,000 international visitors, global delegations and 287 elite exhibitors are filling the base with incredible energy. The five-day event offers high-stakes business networking during the first three days, followed by a thrilling public air show over the weekend. 🇷🇺 🤝 The Russian pavilion is a major highlight at this year's landmark event, bringing together a heavy-hitting lineup of independent corporate innovators . Leading state and private aerospace giants are actively showcasing their latest tactical hardware, advanced unmanned aerial systems (UAVs) and next-generation engineering. It offers a rare, hands-on opportunity to connect face-to-face with representatives and engineering teams from top-tier global powerhouses , including Rosoboronexport, Roscosmos Corporation, Eclipse Group, Aeroscan, Katod and Technodinamika. Everyone is welcome to witness the future of flight! #RussiaSouthAfrica

🎙
Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova’s
answer to a media question
on foreign media insinuations regarding an allegedly deliberate strike by Russian forces on a passenger train that carried several former and current Western politicians and officials
(September 15, 2026)
❓
Question: The Ukrainian and foreign media write that the Russian Armed Forces have allegedly intentionally attacked, as part of the September 13 strikes on targets in Western Ukraine, the trains in which former British Prime Minister Boris Johnson, former CIA Director David Petraeus and officials of several other Western countries travelled from Kiev. Could you comment on this situation?
💬
Maria Zakharova:
Yes, we know about these reports, as well as about a rather strange reaction to them from Ukrainian Foreign Minister
Andrey Sibiga
and
several European politicians and diplomats
.
We would like to say in this connection that unlike the Ukrainian military,
Russia's Armed Forces
do not wage war on civilians
,
target civilian vehicles, or open fire on helpless people
– women, senior citizens and children.
Regarding the strikes mentioned in the media,
our military did deliver them on September 13
, but they targeted
exclusively military facilities and the Kiev regime’s transport and logistics infrastructure
used for military purposes, including in Western Ukraine.
Judging by the monitoring data, these strikes were highly effective and resultative
. We have issued
numerous warnings
that the railway junctions, depots and rolling stock, primarily train engines, which are being actively used to transport Western weapons for the AFU, are
legitimate military targets
.
We will not comment on
the cheap publicity stunt i
nvolving certain political individuals who were in the vicinity of the targeted train with military cargo. The goal of this information ballyhoo
to try to get more military supplies for Zelensky’s regime
by intimidating ordinary Europeans with a mythical
“Russian threat at the NATO’s gate”
.
☝️
It should be noted that
in May
we repeatedly recommended
– and even sent respective notes to the diplomatic corps in Moscow and through our embassies abroad – t
hat foreign citizens, including diplomats and their families, leave Kiev
in connection with the transition of
the Russian Armed Forces
to systematic and consistent strikes against Ukraine’s defence facilities and command and decision-making centres in the capital and other cities of Ukraine.
👉
I would like to remind you that such strikes are delivered
in response to AFU’s terrorist attacks
on civilians and civilian infrastructure in Russia.
We have also long been drawing the attention of all kinds of Western “political tourists” and VIPs that
Zelensky’s regime is cynically using them as a human shield for its military trains
.

item.title: : Embassy of Russia in Germany On September 15, 2026, a ceremony was held to mark the official closure of
item.description: Embassy of Russia in Germany : 🇷🇺 On September 15, 2026, a ceremony was held to mark the official closure of the Russian Consulate General in Bonn . The State Flag of the Russian Federation was lowered to the Russian national anthem, and the plaque bearing the Consulate General’s name was removed . The ceremony was attended by Russian Ambassador to Germany Sergey Nechaev , Russian Consul General in Bonn Oleg Krasnitsky , diplomats from the Embassy and the Consulate General , compatriots and journalists. 💬 In his remarks, Ambassador Sergey Nechaev noted: We are bringing our diplomatic presence on the Rhine to a close. As everyone knows, we have been here for 80 years. Throughout this period, the efforts of Soviet and Russian Leaders, politicians and diplomats laid the foundations for new post-war relations with West Germany, which subsequently grew into good-neighbourliness, partnership and cooperation. A course was set towards historical reconciliation – no easy undertaking for our people after all the suffering and sacrifices they had endured. Nevertheless, we extended a hand to the Germans. Our cooperation developed as it did with no other country. ❗️ As a result of the unfriendly steps by the German authorities, Russia’s Consulate General in Bonn was forced to cease operations . Russia’s diplomatic and consular presence in the region, spanning more than eight decades, has come to an end.

🎙
Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova’s
response to a media question
regarding the continuing Ukrainian attacks and provocations against
the Zaporozhskaya Nuclear Power Plant
(September 15, 2026)
❓
Question: On September 11, Ukrainian forces carried out a series of strikes on tanker trucks transporting diesel fuel for the Zaporozhskaya Nuclear Power Plant’s backup diesel generators. Two Russian servicemen were killed. Several others were injured, some seriously. How would you comment on this situation?
💬
Maria Zakharova:
First and foremost, we extend
our deepest and most sincere condolence
s to the families and loved ones of those killed. We wish the wounded
a speedy recovery
.
Losing ground as persistent battlefield setbacks continue, Ukraine’s authorities and military are taking
increasingly reckless and ruthless action
, attacking Russia’s
Zaporozhskaya Nuclear Power Plant
(
#ZNPP
) and its satellite city of Energodar almost daily.
What makes these attacks and provocations particularly cynical is that they are taking place during
the autumn meetings of the IAEA’s policymaking bodies
, including
the Agency’s landmark 70th General Conference
.
In effect, this is an open challenge to the international community
.
Having long lost touch with reality and gripped by primal fear for its own survival,
the Kiev regime continues to pile up crimes for which it will inevitably be held accountable
.
Atrocities such as the September 11 strikes you mentioned are both
a stark manifestation of Zelensky’s misanthropic ideology
, which is leading him towards collapse, and
a demonstration of the current Ukrainian leaders’ irresponsible attitude towards nuclear safety
.
With Ukrainian forces carrying out intensive, targeted strikes on the infrastructure needed to maintain the ZNPP’s external power supply, replenishing diesel fuel stocks is an essential factor in ensuring the plant’s safe operation.
By ignoring this, Kiev is literally playing with fire, putting the safety of all of Europe at stake
.
***
Furthermore, on September 12,
Ukraine deliberately carried out a series of UAV strikes on the ZNPP’s training centre
, where plant personnel receive training.
We regard the attack on this facility
, which is directly involved in training nuclear specialists,
as
another step aimed at undermining nuclear safety
.
At the same time,
Ukrainian militants continue to strike Energodar’s infrastructure and residential buildings
to exert
psychological pressure
on ZNPP personnel.
Russia has
strongly condemned
these reckless Ukrainian actions at the IAEA. We regularly distribute materials at the Agency about the real state of affairs at the Russian NPP.
❗️
Clearly, by shielding Ukraine’s lawlessness and violence, its Western sponsors are becoming ever more deeply entangled in the threats created by Zelensky.
We expect the IAEA Secretariat and Director General
Rafael Grossi
personally
to
give an unequivocal assessment of of
these developments and
declare the lawlessness of Ukraine’s current leaders unacceptable
.
The AFU is targeting not only Russian professionals but also IAEA Secretariat employees,
whom the Kiev regime is ready to sacrifice at any moment.

🎙️
Comment by Ambassador of Russia to Denmark Vladimir Barbin to the media regarding the incident involving a Russian frigate
The Russian side will
thoroughly investigate
all the circumstances of the incident.
However, this is not the first time that Danish Air Force helicopters have carried out
dangerous manoeuvres near Russian warships
, when they were at sea and outside Denmark’s territorial waters.
For example, in September 2025, during a conversation at the Danish Ministry of Foreign Affairs, I had to draw the attention to the dangerous flyovers and low-altitude hovering carried out on 27 August by a Danish Air Force helicopter over the large anti-submarine vessel ‘Vice-Admiral Kulakov’, when it sailed east of the island of Fehmarn. Such manoeuvres by the Danish military helicopter
posed a risk of collision
and could also have interfered with the operation of the ship’s equipment. Furthermore,
the helicopter’s crew rejected to establish radio contact
with the vessel and
failed to respond to warnings
. In this regard, I demanded that the Danish side should take the necessary measures to prevent the occurrence of similar incidents in the future and handed a note.
This latest incident demonstrates that the communication problems lie not with the Russian Navy’s vessels, but with the Danish side. The Danish side’s attempts to explain the helicopter’s provocative actions against the Russian frigate as ‘routine practice’
give rise to serious concern
about the possible consequences of such recklessness.
Regrettably, the Danish side has no interest – nor has it ever had any – to prevent the situation at sea from escalating and to implement confidence-building measures. Russia’s repeated proposals to explore the possibility of concluding an agreement on the prevention of incidents at sea covering the maritime space and the airspace above these waters have previously been
firmly rejected by the Danish side.
